I will not start from empty. I will do mostly what worked for me before, then push a little where I think it pays. My land is 13.1 mu, and the main stomach of the farm is still wheat-maize. That crop pair feeds the year, so I will give it the better land, more fertilizer, and guaranteed water from the well. Cotton and mungbean I will keep on smaller pieces. Cotton can still bring cash if I manage insects in time, and mungbean does not need as much fertilizer, so it helps me save some money on the lighter ground. I only finished primary school, but after 40 years I know this much: if I cut fertilizer too hard and the stand turns weak, I cannot buy yield back later. So I will keep nitrogen a bit on the safe side, put phosphorus down early, and give potassium to wheat, maize, and cotton where it helps hold the crop. I will also look at what the better growers around me are using. If a hybrid maize and an improved wheat seed did well for people in nearby fields last year, I will use the same type. For tillage, I will keep it simple and practical: rotary till after harvest where it saves labor, and plough the cotton ground once because that land gets tight. Water I will use carefully, but I will not let wheat miss the key irrigation or maize suffer in the jointing and grain-filling time.
